fact: The report says its national institutional maternal and stillbirth rates are consistent with the 2023 vital statistics report; it gives no release date, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Education's EMIS page lists the EMIS Annual Education Census reports for 2019 to 2023 and the 15th School Day Report 2024, built from data the education regions collect from all state and private schools; page dated 2024-01-01, figures cover 2022 to January 2024.

The page states the education regions collect data twice a year from all schools and publish two reports, the Fifteenth School Day Report and the Annual Education Census, with annual census editions listed for 2019 to 2023; page dated 2024-01-01.

The Namibia Statistics Agency published the Namibia Vital Statistics Report 2018-2021 in April 2024 (figures cover births, deaths and marriages registered 2018-2021), stating its vital events are administrative data from the Civil Registration System, extracted from the National Population Registration System held by the Office of the Prime Minister up to 17 February 2022.

The report states the first Vital Statistics Report from civil registration data was published in 2020 (events of 2016 and 2017) and this second edition appeared in April 2024 (events of 2018-2021), made with the Ministries of Home Affairs and of Health.
The report states the first Vital Statistics and Causes of Deaths Report was published in 2020, covering births, deaths and marriages registered in 2016 and 2017.

Namibia Statistics Agency told the SADC workshop that an MoU with the labour ministry (MLIREC) provides for a steering committee and technical working group on data sharing, but no law or MoU yet covers access to immigration records and no administrative statistics are published from them.
